name: authorization-access-control
description: Enforce proper authorization checks, role-based access control, and principle of least privilege across all endpoints
author: community
content:
## Authorization & Access Control

Authentication proves who you are. Authorization decides what you can do. Never confuse them (OWASP A01:2021 Broken Access Control).

### Rules
- Deny by default — require explicit grants, not explicit denials
- Check authorization on EVERY request server-side — never rely on client-side checks alone
- Validate that the authenticated user owns or has access to the requested resource (IDOR prevention)
- Use indirect object references — never expose internal IDs in URLs without access checks
- Implement authorization at the data layer, not just the route/controller layer
- Log all access control failures — they are potential attack attempts
- Disable directory listing on web servers
- Reject requests to sensitive endpoints that lack proper authorization headers

### IDOR Prevention (Insecure Direct Object Reference)
```python
# BAD — trusts user-supplied ID with no ownership check
@app.get("/api/invoices/{invoice_id}")
def get_invoice(invoice_id: int):
    return db.get_invoice(invoice_id)

# GOOD — verifies the user owns this resource
@app.get("/api/invoices/{invoice_id}")
def get_invoice(invoice_id: int, user = Depends(get_current_user)):
    invoice = db.get_invoice(invoice_id)
    if invoice.user_id != user.id:
        raise HTTPException(403)
    return invoice
```

### Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
- Define roles with minimum necessary permissions
- Map permissions to roles, not directly to users
- Check permissions, not role names — `has_permission('edit_post')` not `role == 'admin'`
- Support role hierarchies if needed, but keep them shallow (max 3-4 levels)
- Review and audit role assignments periodically

### API Authorization
- Protect every API endpoint — including internal/admin endpoints
- Use scoped tokens (OAuth2 scopes, API key scopes) to limit what a token can do
- Implement function-level access control — not just resource-level
- Return 403 Forbidden (not 404) only when the user is authenticated but unauthorized; use 401 for unauthenticated
- For multi-tenant systems: enforce tenant isolation at the query level, not just the application level

### Common Pitfalls
- Hiding UI elements is NOT authorization — always enforce server-side
- Checking roles in frontend code is for UX only, not security
- Path traversal in file operations: validate and canonicalize all file paths
- Mass assignment: explicitly allowlist which fields a user can update
- Privilege escalation: verify role changes require admin authorization

### Middleware Pattern
```javascript
// Express middleware example
function requirePermission(permission) {
  return (req, res, next) => {
    if (!req.user) return res.sendStatus(401);
    if (!req.user.permissions.includes(permission)) return res.sendStatus(403);
    next();
  };
}

app.delete('/api/posts/:id', requirePermission('delete_post'), deletePost);
```
